records.note: no prison-housing data found — two search rounds incl. Slovak-language queries (transrodový väzeň, ženská väznica, Leopoldov, Hrnčiarovce, Inakosť) surfaced only republished foreign trans-prisoner cases in Slovak outlets (hlavnespravy.sk 14 Jan 2024 and pravdive.eu both re-report the US Georgia Phillips State Prison case; plenum.sk, standard.sk re-report US policy) and generic prison guides (humanrightsguide.sk cell-placement page); no Slovakia-specific placement policy, special custody unit, solitary/administrative-segregation practice or court ruling on trans prisoner housing is documented, and the ECtHR HUDOC database returns no trans-prisoner case against Slovakia. The regional framework (CPT 33rd General Report standard on transgender persons in prison, CPT/Inf (2024) 16) applies, but no Slovak application of it was found.

adds.title: Trăind de gardă/ Deținut transgender – dublu condamnat în închisoare de către „oamenii cu epoleți”
adds.summary: Moldovan investigative outlet Ziarul de Gardă (15 June 2024) documents the four-year detention of Igor Brumarețchi, a transgender man (registered female at birth in 1972, documents changed to male in 2007), who served his sentence in Moldova's penitentiary system, mostly at Penitentiary No. 6 in Soroca. He says he was held alone in unsanitary, rat-infested cells — including for long periods in the disciplinary isolation unit ('izolator disciplinar') — supposedly for his own safety, while his request for sector 12 (the unit for detainees requiring protection) was refused. He describes staff humiliation: forced strip body searches, 'go to the gynaecologist' calls over the intercom, opening his bathroom door, and calling him 'Natașa' at roll-call, and says only self-harm and hunger strikes got him heard. The National Penitentiary Administration (ANP) replied that he was detained alone 'at his own written request' and without any rights being violated, and that the discrimination claims were unconfirmed; Brumarețchi says he will sue in Moldovan courts and the ECtHR, and ZdG has notified the Ombudsman and GENDERDOC-M. Outcome: de facto placement of a trans detainee by birth sex in the men's system with prolonged solitary-style isolation, refused protection-ward placement, and no special-unit option.

adds.title: Deținuți ai prejudecăților în instituțiile de stat. Persoane LGBT+, la un pas de suicid. Povestea tragică a unui locuitor al satului Dubna
adds.summary: Observatorul de Nord (7 April 2025) corroborates the same case: Igor Brumarețchi from Dubna village (Soroca district) spent three years locked alone in a cell at Penitentiary No. 6 in Soroca, fully isolated from other detainees and humiliated by prison staff on grounds of sexual orientation, which brought him to the edge of suicide. The piece states the authorities admit homophobia still persists in state institutions and say they are training staff and preparing stricter penalties for discrimination and harassment; the full investigation appeared on anticoruptie.md. Confirms the solitary-style isolation placement practice for a trans detainee in Moldovan prison No. 6 as of 2025.

records.note: No statutory trans-prisoner placement rule found for Moldova; the only documented case (Igor Brumarețchi, a trans man, Penitentiary No. 6 Soroca, c. 2020-2024) shows de facto placement in the men's system with prolonged solitary-style isolation presented by the ANP as his own requested arrangement, refused protection-ward (sector 12) placement, and staff harassment (ZdG, 15 Jun 2024; Observatorul de Nord, 7 Apr 2025). No special custody unit for trans detainees and no administrative-segregation rule are documented.

adds.title: Prisons luxembourgeoises : Les détenus gays et transgenres sont protégés
adds.summary: L'essentiel (26 August 2015), reporting Justice Minister Félix Braz's parliamentary answer to LSAP MP Cécile Hemmen, documents that Luxembourg prisons place inmates who disclose or openly show LGBT/trans identity so they are sheltered from reprisals, threats or attacks by other prisoners, with trans-detainee situations handled case by case (the administration gathers all available information on the prisoner); such cases are described as 'exceptional'. Requests by LGBT detainees to be placed in an ordinary section are generally granted, and the minister warned against solutions that would stigmatise or isolate these detainees. A 1989 grand-ducal regulation requires staff to address detainees by surname, and penitentiary staff honour a detainee's chosen 'Monsieur'/'Madame' form of address. The Justice Ministry kept no statistics on LGBT prisoners (disclosure cannot be compelled without illegal privacy interference), and the planned Uerschterhaff prison (Sanem) was designed with multiple sections so detainees could be separated by sex, personality, grounds of detention and, among these, sexual orientation. Outcome: placement follows disclosed identity/need on a case-by-case basis with no codified birth-sex rule and no documented special custody unit or solitary/administrative-segregation practice for trans prisoners in Luxembourg.

records.note: Luxembourg has no codified trans-prisoner placement rule; the only documented placement-policy source is the Justice Minister's Aug 2015 parliamentary answer (L'essentiel 26 Aug 2015): disclosing LGBT/trans detainees are placed for their protection, trans cases handled case by case and described as exceptional, requests to remain in ordinary sections generally granted, chosen title/address honoured, and no statistics kept. No special custody unit, solitary/administrative-segregation practice, or court ruling on trans prisoner placement was found.

no prison-housing data found — Catalan/French/English searches for trans prisoners at Andorra's sole prison (Centre Penitenciari de la Comella) returned nothing trans-specific; general prison coverage (SPA reporting on limited isolation practice, planned CPT visit to Comella in 2027) contains no trans-detainee placement, special custody unit, or solitary/administrative-segregation content.
